proposals.evidence: DEDR3376(a) explicitly gives Tamil tūṅku ‘sleep, slumber’ as well as hang/swing. Survey tūngə matches this stem with its voiced stop and final central vowel retained. The annotation3276 is an unrelated sobbing entry, and3291 tuñcu is only a questioned broader comparison. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR156(a) gives Tamil appaṉ, Malayalam appan, Kannada appa and Kodagu appë father. The selected survey appa/appan/appe responses retain the same locally elicited father sense; minority-lect extensions are comparative. This nursery/honorific family does not by itself distinguish shared inheritance from regional diffusion, and other languages’ mother/aunt senses are not substituted. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR4616 explicitly gives Tamil makaṉ and Malayalam makan/mōn son, Kannada maga/makan, Tulu mage and Toda mox child/son. The selected southern survey makan/magan/maga/mahan-type responses preserve the family, including k/g/h variation and nasalized or nasal-cluster lect forms. These minority-lect assignments are comparative proposals; ambiguous contractions and longer compounds are excluded. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR3582 gives Tamil naṭa, Malayalam naṭakka, Kannada naḍe/naḍi, Kodagu naḍa- and Tulu naḍapuni to walk. These complete southern survey naḍa/naḍi/naḍakk-/naḍap- forms preserve the stem and source inflection; the Kudiya naḍapu comparison follows intransitive Tulu naḍapuni, not Kannada causative naḍapu. Longer or opaque responses are excluded. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.
